PROJECT TITLE:RESTORATION OF LAKE ONTARIO NATIVE FISH SPECIESPROJECT PERIOD: 06/01/2022-05/31/2023ANTHROPOGENIC ACTIVITIES HAVE GREATLY IMPACTED FISH POPULATIONS IN THE GREAT LAKES. OF ALL THE GREAT LAKES, FISH POPULATIONS IN LAKE ONTARIO HAVE BEEN IMPACTED THE MOST SEVERELY, INCLUDING THE EXTIRPATION OF ATLANTIC SALMON AND DEEPWATER COREGONINES, SUCH AS BLOATER, AND MAJOR DECLINES IN LAKE STURGEON, DEEPWATER SCULPIN, LAKE HERRING AND AMERICAN EEL. LOSS OF SPAWNING HABITAT AND PERHAPS OVERFISHING ARE THOUGHT TO BE THE MAJOR CAUSES FOR THE LOSS OF ATLANTIC SALMON AND LAKE STURGEON, WHEREAS INVASIVE SPECIES SUCH AS ALEWIFE AND RAINBOW SMELT ARE CONSIDERED TO HAVE LED THE DECLINE OF COREGONIDS AND DEEPWATER SCULPIN, AS WELL AS ATLANTIC SALMON (I.E. THIAMINE DEFICIENCY). BECAUSE OF THE COMPLEXITIES ASSOCIATED WITH THE EXTIRPATION OR DECLINE OF NATIVE FISH SPECIES IN THE GREAT LAKES, THERE IS NO SINGLE REMEDY SUITABLE FOR THE RESTORATION OF ALL SPECIES. UNFORTUNATELY, ALTHOUGH ALEWIFE POPULATIONS IN LAKE ONTARIO ARE DECLINING, THERE ARE NO DEEPWATER COREGONIDS REMAINING IN THE LAKE TO ENABLE NATURAL RECOVERY. CONSEQUENTLY, THE RESTORATION OF DEEPWATER COREGONIDS, AS WELL AS EXTIRPATED ATLANTIC SALMON, MUST AT LEAST INITIALLY RELY ON HATCHERY REARED FISH. THE FOCUS OF THIS NATIVE SPECIES RESTORATION EFFORT WILL BE LAKE ONTARIO AND THE ST. LAWRENCE RIVER, WHICH SUPPORTS USGS PROGRAM PRIORITIES AND REQUIREMENTS.THIS EFFORT WILL CONSIST OF THREE SEPARATE THRUSTS GEARED AT RESTORING ATLANTIC SALMON, AND COREGONIDS, IN LAKE ONTARIO AND THE ST. LAWRENCE RIVER THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW AND INNOVATIVE RESTORATION TECHNIQUES.DEEPWATER COREGONIDS: FACILITATE THE RE-INTRODUCTION OF EXTIRPATED DEEPWATER COREGONINE FISHES IN LAKE ONTARIO THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW AND INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES WHILE FOLLOWING PROPER DISEASE PROTOCOLS WHEN TRANSFERRING EGGS TO ISOLATION FACILITIES.CISCO: FACILITATE THE RECOVERY OF CISCO IN LAKE ONTARIO THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW AND INNOVATIVE REARING TECHNIQUES AND THE EVALUATION OF THE SUITABILITY OF HISTORIC SPAWNING SITES AS STOCKING LOCATIONS.PLANNED PRODUCTS AND DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS- THE MOST OBVIOUS PRODUCT OF THE COLLABORATIVE EFFORT WILL BE THE ANNUAL NUMBER OF FISH THAT ARE REARED AND EXPERIMENTALLY RELEASED FOR RESTORATION PURPOSES AND INFORMATION ABOUT THE SUCCESS OF THOSE RELEASES AND ADULTS RETURNING TO RELEASE SITES. PROJECT TITLE: IMPACT OF HABITAT QUALITY ON PLANT AND AVIAN SPECIES IN BEAVER LAKE AREAPROJECT PERIOD: AUGUST 30, 2023, THROUGH SEPTEMBER 30, 2024PROJECT ABSTRACT: HABITAT QUALITY PLAYS A CRUCIAL ROLE IN DETERMINING THE PLANT AND AVIAN SPECIES DIVERSITY IN AN ECOSYSTEM, AND EFFORTS TO PROTECT AND RESTORE HIGH-QUALITY HABITATS ARE ESSENTIAL FOR PRESERVING BIODIVERSITY. WITH AN OVERARCHING GOAL OF AIDING THE U.S. ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) TO MAKE INFORMED CONSERVATION AND LAND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS, RECIPIENT PROPOSES TO SURVEY 30 SITES IN THE NORTHEAST REGION OF BEAVER LAKE: 1) TO CONDUCT BOTANICAL SURVEYS AND HABITAT ASSESSMENTS TO DETERMINE PRESENCE ABSENCE OF STATE AND FEDERALLY LISTED AND PROPOSED PLANT SPECIES AS WELL AS HABITAT QUALITY   AND 2) TO CONDUCT BIRD SURVEYS DURING SPRING MIGRATION, FALL MIGRATION, AND THE BREEDING SEASON TO DOCUMENT PRESENCE, DENSITY, AND DISTRIBUTION OF LISTED SPECIES AND REGIONAL SPECIES OF CONCERN. IN ADDITION TO OBTAINING CRUCIAL DATA FOR LAND MANAGEMENT THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE TRAINING TO GRADUATE STUDENTS IN ECOLOGICAL FIELD METHODS DURING DATA COLLECTION, AND SCIENCE COMMUNICATION VIA CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS AND MANUSCRIPT WRITING. THE SITES WILL REPRESENT AN EQUAL NUMBER OF HIGH-QUALITY, MODERATELY DISTURBED, AND HIGHLY DISTURBED HABITATS WITHIN THE BEAVER LAKE AREA. A COMBINATION OF MEANDER SEARCHES, TRANSECTS, AND QUADRATS WILL BE USED TO GATHER QUANTITATIVE DATA ON HABITAT QUALITY AND SPATIAL LOCATION OF THE FEDERALLY AND STATE LISTED SPECIES OF CONCERN. WHEN A STATE OR FEDERALLY LISTED SPECIES IS FOUND, GPS COORDINATES WILL BE TAKEN, AND A POPULATION SIZE ESTIMATE WILL BE RECORDED. IF THE POPULATION IS SMALL, GPS CENTER POINT AND RADIUS THAT ENCLOSES THE POPULATION WILL BE TAKEN. FOR A LARGE POPULATION ( 6.25 M), MULTIPLE POINTS AROUND THE PERIMETER OF THE POPULATION WILL BE RECORDED SO THAT A POLYGON CAN BE DRAWN. VOUCHER SPECIMENS WILL BE COLLECTED OF TARGET AND UNKNOWN SPECIES. ALL PLANTS COLLECTED IN THE FIELD WILL BE PRESSED, DRIED, IDENTIFIED TO SPECIES WHEN POSSIBLE AND TO SUBSPECIES VARIETY WHEN APPLICABLE, AND DEPOSITED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS HERBARIUM (UARK). IF ENOUGH MATERIAL IS COLLECTED FOR MORE THAN ONE SPECIMEN, THE SECOND SPECIMEN WILL BE OFFERED TO THE ARKANSAS NATURAL HERITAGE COMMISSION HERBARIUM (ANHC). LABEL DATA FOR EACH COLLECTION WILL INCLUDE THE COLLECTOR(S) NAME, COLLECTOR NUMBER, DATE OF COLLECTION, GPS LOCATION AND DETAILED DIRECTIONS TO THE SITE, A BRIEF HABITAT DESCRIPTION WITH ASSOCIATED SPECIES FOUND IN THE IMMEDIATE AREA, AND ANY FEATURE OF THE PLANT THAT MAY BE LOST ONCE THE PLANT IS PRESSED AND DRIED, SUCH AS PLANT HABIT, PLANT HEIGHT, FLOWER COLOR, AND FRUIT COLOR. NOMENCLATURE WILL FOLLOW WEAKLEY (2022).
